subject: SFTP export, residency and prompt/response IP — DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Rachel Torres <privacy@carenexus.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-23T16:12:00Z
Subject: SFTP export, residency and prompt/response IP — DPA addendum request

Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to procurement we need a short written confirmation on a few privacy items so our legal and security teams can sign off. High-level asks below — can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these operationally (and point us to the clause language you would add to the DPA)?

1) No-training / no-model-improvement: CareNexus requires that any interaction data (including prompts and system context) is not used to improve or retrain Redwood models or third-party models. We understand some providers offer an operational "no-train" commitment. Can Redwood provide an auditable commitment and an operational description of how that is enforced?

2) Prompt/response IP: We need clarity on whether prompts and generated responses are treated as customer data/IP. Specifically: will CareNexus retain ownership of outputs and are there any restrictions on Redwood's use of customer-generated outputs for derivates, analytics, or internal model tuning?

3) EU residency / export: We must ensure EU-customer data remains in the EU. If Redwood offers SFTP export as a contractual export path (for on-demand bulk exports), can you confirm the location of the SFTP host (EU region) and any export controls? We also need to understand KMS key residency (can we BYOK in an EU KMS?).

4) Subprocessors: Please provide the list of subprocessors that will have access to raw prompts/responses (not just telemetry). A short dataflow map showing where customer inputs travel would be very helpful.

Attached is a redline template from our legal team; if you can return a proposed DPA addendum and dataflow map that addresses the points above, we can move to signature. If easier, we can take a 30-min call to walk through the requirements — Rachel (privacy) and Tom (legal) will both join.

Thanks,
Rachel Torres
Head of Privacy, CareNexus
privacy@carenexus.com

Attachments: CareNexus_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Torres <privacy@carenexus.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SFTP export, residency and prompt/response IP — DPA addendum request

Hi Rachel / Tom,

Thanks — good, concise list. Short answers up front and proposed next steps below: 

- No-training: We can provide a contractual operational commitment: inputs and generated outputs for customer-managed endpoints (hosted with dedicated capacity) will not be used to improve Redwood models. For hosted customers that require stronger isolation, Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private provide additional guarantees (isolated GPU pools, optional BYOK). We will provide explicit clause language for the DPA addendum.

- Prompt/response IP: Redwood’s standard position is that customers retain rights to their inputs and outputs. We will propose language that explicitly states outputs and prompts are Customer Data and that Redwood will not use outputs to create derivatives beyond what is required for logging/telemetry (and only with anonymization and aggregated analytics, unless you contract otherwise). I will mark the proposed redline.

- EU residency / SFTP export: We offer an EU-hosted SFTP export endpoint (sftp-eu.redwood.example) for bulk export and a per-tenant routing policy that pins traffic to EU regions. We can support BYOK in EU KMS or use Redwood-managed EU keys; I will flag options in the addendum.

- Subprocessors: I'll attach a short dataflow map and a list of subprocessors that have access to raw prompts/responses. Note that some monitoring/logging partners only receive aggregated telemetry; we will call out who has access to raw text.

Next steps: I attached a draft DPA addendum (DPA_addendum_Redwood_v2.pdf) with suggested clauses for no-training, output ownership, and export/KMS options. David will follow up with the technical export/dataflow artefact. Can we schedule a 30-min call on Tue 29 Aug at 14:00 UTC to align? If that doesn't work we'll propose alternatives.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Attachments: DPA_addendum_Redwood_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Torres <privacy@carenexus.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: SFTP export, residency and prompt/response IP — technical notes

Hi all,

Following Evelyn's note — here are the technical commitments and how they map to the proposed DPA clauses. Happy to discuss on the call.

1) Enforcement of no-training:
- For "no-training" tenants we offer tagging + routing: requests are tagged at the edge with tenant no-train metadata and routed to inference fleets where telemetry collection paths for training are disabled.
- KV cache and ephemeral session data are stored in per-tenant volumes that are not forwarded to model training pipelines.
- We maintain an audit trail showing the routing and the telemetry flags; this is available for SOC2/incident review.

2) Prompt/response custody:
- Raw prompts/responses remain encrypted in transit and at rest. Retention is configurable per tenant; default retention for hosted is 30 days but can be set to 0 (ephemeral) for strict customers.
- Outputs will be marked as Customer Data in the DPA addendum — we will not index outputs into any shared model artifacts for training.

3) SFTP export & EU residency:
- SFTP export endpoint: sftp-eu.redwood.example (SFTP over SFTP-SSH). Exports are placed into a tenant-specific directory scoped to EU.
- Export process supports encryption using a tenant public key; we also support pushing to your SFTP host if you prefer.
- For live inference routing we can pin to: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1.

4) KMS / key residency:
- BYOK: we support customer-managed keys in EU KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) via our key-wrapping flow.
- Redwood-managed EU keys are available if BYOK is not required.

5) Subprocessors:
- Short list (access to raw prompts/responses): CloudStoragePartner EU (s3-compatible storage in EU), AuditLogsCo (on-demand log retrieval for SOC2 audits).
- MonitoringCorp receives only aggregated metrics (no raw prompts). Full list will be in the addendum.

Attachment: dataflow_map_carenexus.xlsx — shows the path: customer app -> edge -> eu inference fleet -> (optional) SFTP export or tenant storage -> backup/archival (EU).

Questions for CareNexus before the call: retention window required, desired KMS option (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), and whether you prefer push-to-your-SFTP or Redwood-placed export.

Thanks,
David
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Attachments: dataflow_map_carenexus.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Tom Li <legal@carenexus.com>

Cc: Rachel Torres <privacy@carenexus.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SFTP export, residency and prompt/response IP — DPA addendum request

Evelyn / David,

Thanks for the quick responses and the draft. A few follow-ups before the call: 

- Can you share the exact clause text you propose for the no-training commitment (we prefer redact-ready language we can drop into our DPA redline). Specifically: the scope ("inputs and outputs used for model training"), the carveouts (if any) for aggregated telemetry, and the auditability language (what logs we can review).

- Please confirm the outputs/IP sentence explicitly: we need a sentence that states "Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Customer Data and Customer Outputs; Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to develop or improve models without Customer's prior written consent." If you already have that in the draft PDF, highlight the exact section.

- Subprocessors: we need a brief note on whether any of the listed subprocessors are likely to change within 90 days and an escalation contact for procurement should we need an alternate.

- DocuSign: once we agree the addendum we will need a DocuSign-ready copy. If you can send a DocuSign link with the final PDF we can route internally quickly.

On availability: Tue 29 Aug 14:00 UTC works for us.
